v1.notes: Reproduces (not validates) Guo et al. 2026 obstructed-sky ratios from the USGS Gale 1 m DEM at MSL waypoint positions (MAE 2.0 pp over 15 periods, r=0.94). Metric definition chosen post hoc among 3 readings. Dose-drop RMSE 4.3 pp with our ROS vs 1.8 pp with the paper ROS; the largest miss is Maria Gordon Notch (narrow valley: ours 25.66% vs paper 37.9%). 8 events, one rover, one GCR model: indicative only.

v2.notes: Pandolf+Santee x g-ratio vs IST-2 Mark III suited VO2 (digitized Fig. 36 trend lines, Norcross 2010), 5 gravities x 4 grades, subject mass 80.7 kg, suit 121 kg, speed 0.765 m/s (paper range 0.56-0.97). Model underpredicts at 0.12-0.17 g (measured VO2 has a gravity-independent floor) and is within about +-14% at 0.22-0.32 g. 0.38 g is an extrapolation beyond the 0.32 g maximum; no data there.

oversubscribed.notes: All 12 stations, base PR-1, available EVA time 120-240 min via EVA_CUT (330 - available), 200 seeded scenarios. B = nearest-first with the same hard-rule checker. Science values are the team STM heuristic; single site; B is a generous but not the only human baseline.

v3.manualPlanningRef: no published figure found for hours of manual EVA traverse planning per EVA; only lead times (D-RATS 2010 planning began ~12 months before the field test; BASALT traverse targets were chosen months ahead from satellite imagery)
v3.notes: gale-v1 real DEM, base PR-1, 200 seeded scenarios (3-6 of 12 stations, start 08:00-11:00 LTST, sol 412 with assumed Ls 240). Nearest-first WITH the same safety check selected exactly the same station set as Marswalk in every scenario (ratio 1.0): in this tight-limit site the safety rules, not the stop-order optimisation, decide the outcome. The naive slope-only plan visits ALL requested targets and breaks >=1 hard rule in 99.5% of scenarios. Science values are the team STM heuristic. See v3_impact/README.md.

v5.notes: Compares (does not validate) the radiation.ts Guo-2015-form dose model with measured MSL RAD absorbed dose (PDS PPI RDR, detector E plastic = like-for-like; B silicon is ~4% higher) and REMS pressure for 131 sampled sols. Measured diurnal barometric coefficient is about half the published values (timing stamps in the RDR are unreliable). P_ref 750 Pa is ~160 Pa below the Ls 240 REMS mean; dose depends strongly on solar-cycle epoch (E 167-296 uGy/day at Ls 240 across 2012-2024). One rover, one site; see v5_rad_dose/README.md.

v4.notes: 24 single-destination walks on gale-v1 (12 GO, 12 NO-GO by the engine). Independent Python checker (own slope, edge grade, ray line-of-sight, radius, simple time model; no engine code) and blind Claude AI judges (read only the rules + per-step evidence packets; engine verdicts hidden). AI judges use packet values that include engine-derived per-step times (incl. heat rests), line of sight and shelter minutes, so they verify rule application, not the underlying models; the independent checker verifies geometry and line of sight independently. Re-run after the radio-relay fix (every masted shelter relays). The single disagreement (W02) is a safe-side engine NO-GO: the engine judged its heat-aware route (radio gap 0.22 min over the limit) while the shortest-time path in the packet passes; the engine does not yet try alternative paths before NO-GO. See v4_crosscheck/README.md.
